selected_problem: Arbitrary complex repository synthesis remains UNRESOLVED. Fresh-main inspection found that WorkspaceService.manifest declared maxFiles as a hard repository-observation budget, but recursive unwinding could append one additional sibling file at every ancestor after a deep child filled the budget. A direct reproduction with maxFiles=1 returned seven files, so downstream repository summary, semantic graph seeding and context recovery could receive more repository entries than the declared bound.

execution.route_basis: The latest canonical main still exposes native complex synthesis as unresolved. The fresh code reality contains one narrow, directly falsifiable repository-observation budget defect in the existing manifest traversal, so source-contract replay narrows it to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without prescribing a new synthesis architecture or forcing mode rotation.

changes: WorkspaceService.manifest now re-checks maxFiles at the start of every directory-entry iteration, including after a recursive child returns.
Recursive unwinding can no longer append sibling files after the manifest budget has already been reached.
Existing hidden-directory filters, file metadata shape and traversal semantics remain otherwise unchanged.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: REPRODUCED against fresh main: a six-level nested directory with one sibling file at each ancestor and maxFiles=1 returned 7 manifest entries instead of 1.

truth_boundaries: Arbitrary complex repository synthesis remains UNRESOLVED. This makes manifest maxFiles truthful under recursive unwinding; it does not prove semantic sufficiency of the bounded repository observation.

Manifest traversal is still depth-first and may omit later peer subtrees once the file-count budget is legitimately exhausted; fair or goal-aware repository coverage remains a separate selection-quality question.
Initial semantic seed priority across many otherwise admissible files remains a separate selection-quality question.
BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: GitHub's merge REST endpoint still lacks an atomic expected-base-SHA precondition, so external GET-to-PUT base races remain outside client-side elimination.
